summary: The biggest new money in communications is AI traffic between data centers: Lumen has about $13B of AI fiber contracts and Ciena expects more than $10B of backlog, which is more certain than anything in consumer telecom. Space is the second flow: SpaceX (SPCX) closed at about a $2.26T market value on Oct 5, 2026, Starlink Mobile reached about 22M monthly users by August, and Amazon is spending to catch up (Leo plus an $11.6B Globalstar deal). All 56 state BEAD broadband plans are now approved, so rural fiber money moves from paperwork to construction. Open RAN and AI-RAN are still trials; radio equipment sales were still falling as of Q2.

innovations.name: Direct to phone satellite
innovations.what: Satellites that talk straight to normal cell phones, so coverage works where there are no towers. Today it is mostly texting; voice and data are next.
innovations.stage_why: Starlink Mobile is used at scale through carriers like T-Mobile (about 22M monthly users by August 2026), but mostly for text and light data. Broadband to phones from space (AST SpaceMobile, Starlink V2) is still ramping: AST had launched 13 BlueBirds by Aug 5, 2026 and its target of about 45 has slipped.

evidence.approvals: SpaceX agreed to buy 50 MHz of EchoStar S-band spectrum plus global satellite licenses for about $17B, its first owned satellite-to-phone spectrum in the US (2025). AST SpaceMobile holds FCC authority for its direct to cell system and uses partner carrier spectrum.
evidence.money: Amazon agreed on April 14, 2026 to buy Globalstar for about $11.6B ($90 per share), expected to close in 2027. Apple earlier put $1.1B into Globalstar plus a 20% stake for iPhone satellite features. AST raised $1.15B of 1.625% convertible notes in July 2026 and had $3.7B pro forma cash at June 30, 2026.
evidence.revenue: Starlink Mobile: 10M monthly active users as of March 2026, about 22M monthly users by August 2026; SpaceX targets 25M by end of 2026. AST SpaceMobile Q2 2026 revenue $31.5M (missed estimates) with operating expenses of $329.1M; 2026 guide $150M to $200M, Q4 weighted; contracted commitments above $1.2B.

spreads_to.use: Remote patient monitoring and emergency SOS in rural areas without cell coverage.
Tracking equipment, trucks and livestock sensors off the grid.
Backup communications for first responders and the military; AST has US government contracts.

innovations.bottleneck: Mobile satellite spectrum and launch capacity. SpaceX controls the most launches and now owns EchoStar's S-band; Amazon is buying Globalstar's spectrum.

next_milestone.event: AST launches BlueBirds 14 to 16 (shipped to Cape Canaveral Sep 30, 2026) and moves toward about 45 satellites; Starlink Mobile reaches its 25M user target
next_milestone.timing: Q4 2026 for the next AST launch; end of 2026 for the Starlink target; early 2027 for broad AST US service

innovations.thesis_broken_if: AST misses its 2026 revenue guide and its launch cadence slips again, while Starlink's monthly active mobile users stop growing toward 25M.

innovations.name: Low earth orbit broadband
innovations.what: Thousands of satellites in low orbit that deliver home, business, airline and ship internet with fiber-like speed. Starlink proved the model; Amazon Leo is the first serious challenger.
innovations.stage_why: Starlink has more than 13M subscribers (August 2026) and generated $11.4B of revenue in 2025. Amazon Leo only reached its commercial threshold in July 2026 and plans consumer service first in the US, Canada, UK, France and Germany, so competition is just beginning.

evidence.cost: Starlink average revenue per user fell 18% to $81 a month (S-1, 2026) as it moved into cheaper markets, a sign the service is going mass market.
evidence.approvals: BEAD rural broadband rules let satellite win about 20% of locations and over $1B, but NTIA asked states in 2026 to remove up to half of satellite-awarded locations.
evidence.money: SpaceX IPO on June 12, 2026 (SPCX) targeted a $75B raise at a $1.75T valuation; the stock closed at $171.09 on Oct 5, 2026, about $2.26T. Amazon Leo had more than 390 satellites in orbit by July 2, 2026, plus distribution deals with NBN Australia, DIRECTV Latin America and Sky Brasil.
evidence.revenue: Starlink revenue $11.4B in 2025, 61% of SpaceX's $18.7B; SpaceX lost $4.28B in Q1 2026. SpaceX reported more than 13M consumer Starlink subscribers by August 2026. Amazon Leo enterprise beta (Apr 8, 2026) included Verizon, AT&T, Vodafone, JetBlue and NASA.

spreads_to.use: In-flight and at-sea internet; JetBlue is an Amazon Leo beta user.
Military communications and Starshield-style government constellations.
Connectivity for remote rigs, mines and pipelines.

innovations.bottleneck: Launch capacity, controlled mostly by SpaceX (which also launches some competitors), plus radio spectrum rights.

next_milestone.event: Amazon Leo consumer beta in its first five countries and SpaceX's first quarterly reports as a public company

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Starlink subscriber growth slows while ARPU keeps falling, so revenue stalls and the $1.75T valuation has nothing to grow into.

innovations.name: Fiber to the home buildout
innovations.what: Replacing copper and cable lines with fiber to homes and businesses. Fiber is the network that also feeds 5G towers and Wi-Fi.
innovations.stage_why: AT&T and Verizon are each adding millions of fiber homes a year and spending tens of billions on fiber deals. The innovation is in scale and consolidation, not new technology.

evidence.approvals: BEAD (the $42.45B federal broadband program): NTIA approved all 56 state and territory final proposals by Aug 25, 2026 and says it saved about $21B versus original plans. A September 2026 policy notice sets rules for what states do with the remaining money. Satellite awards were cut back earlier in 2026.
evidence.money: AT&T committed $250B over 2026 to 2030 and targets more than 60M fiber endpoints, building at a 4M per year run rate by end of 2026. AT&T closed its $5.75B purchase of Lumen's consumer fiber (1M plus subscribers, 4M plus passings). Verizon closed its about $20B Frontier deal in January 2026, reaching about 30M fiber passings.
evidence.revenue: Corning Optical Communications Q1 2026 sales $1.85B, up 36%, mainly from data center demand. Verizon targets 35M to 40M passings over time.

spreads_to.use: Home telehealth, remote monitoring and imaging transfer need symmetric fiber upload speeds.
Fiber backhaul feeds 5G and future 6G small cells.
Fiber-ready homes and buildings command higher rents and values.

innovations.bottleneck: Skilled construction crews and permits, plus fiber and connectivity supply that is now competing with AI data centers (Corning signed big hyperscaler deals).

next_milestone.event: BEAD construction starts and subgrantee contracts; AT&T Q3 2026 fiber net adds (Oct 21) and Verizon Q3 (Oct 26)

innovations.thesis_broken_if: AT&T and Verizon cut fiber build targets to protect cash as the 10-year Treasury yield stays above 5%.

innovations.name: AI data center interconnect (long haul fiber and coherent optics)
innovations.what: High-capacity fiber routes and optical gear that link AI data centers to each other across cities and states, so several campuses can train and serve models as one system.
innovations.stage_why: Hyperscalers are signing multiyear, multibillion-dollar fiber and optical deals, and Ciena's hyperscaler revenue is over half its sales. The buildout is early: Lumen plans to more than triple its fiber miles by 2031.

evidence.money: Lumen has nearly $13B of Private Connectivity Fabric contracts with hyperscalers and AI firms, including Anthropic, and plans to grow to about 47M fiber miles by 2028 and 58M by 2031. Corning fiber deals: Meta up to $6B, NVIDIA up to $3.2B, plus Amazon (2026).
evidence.revenue: Ciena fiscal Q3 2026 (reported Sep 3, 2026): revenue $1.67B, up 37%; hyperscaler-linked 53% of revenue; backlog $8.5B, expected above $10B by fiscal year end. Nokia Q2 2026 AI and cloud customer sales EUR 446M, more than doubled, with optical networks up 19%.

spreads_to.use: Fiber routes often follow power lines; utilities lease rights of way.
Low-latency routes for trading and cloud-based banking.
Hospital systems moving imaging and records to cloud AI rely on the same backbone.

innovations.bottleneck: Fiber supply (Corning), coherent optical modules and lasers (Ciena, Nokia/Infinera, Coherent, Lumentum), and rights of way that take years to secure.

next_milestone.event: Ciena fiscal Q4 results with backlog above $10B; Lumen Q3 update on PCF deals

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Hyperscalers slow new campus construction and Ciena's backlog stops growing.

innovations.name: Open RAN, AI-RAN and 6G
innovations.what: Cell networks built from software and standard computers with open interfaces, so carriers can mix vendors and run AI on the same hardware. 6G is the next standard, designed around AI and sensing.
innovations.stage_why: AT&T carries over 50% of traffic on open-capable hardware, but true multi-vendor open RAN and GPU-based AI-RAN are in field trials. On Sep 16, 2026 Nokia said eight more operators (A1, Chunghwa, du, e&, Mobily, stc, TPG and Zain Saudi) were running proofs of concept or field trials, on top of T-Mobile, SoftBank, Indosat and NTT DOCOMO. Trials are not orders yet; 6G specs target 2029.

evidence.cost: Nokia claims its AI-RAN platform can more than double spectral efficiency by 2028 (company claim).
evidence.approvals: 3GPP's first implementable 6G specifications are targeted for 2029, aligned with T-Mobile and Qualcomm 6G commercialization plans.
evidence.money: NVIDIA invested $1B in Nokia for about a 3% stake (October 2025) to build AI-RAN on its ARC-Pro platform. AT&T's $250B five-year plan includes 5G and open RAN. Omdia estimates the cumulative AI-RAN market above $200B by 2030 (forecast).
evidence.revenue: Radio equipment spend is still shrinking: Ericsson Q2 2026 net sales fell 6% y/y and its Networks unit fell 8% to about $3.4B. AT&T reported in March 2026 that more than 50% of its traffic is on open-capable hardware, aiming for 70% by late 2026.

spreads_to.use: Private 5G and AI-RAN networks in factories, ports and warehouses.
6G sensing and low-latency links for connected vehicles.
Trusted, non-Chinese open networks for allied militaries.

innovations.bottleneck: Carrier capex, which is flat to down, and the RAN software and integration skill held by Ericsson and Nokia.

next_milestone.event: Ericsson Q3 2026 report (radio sales trend), then Nokia and NVIDIA AI-RAN pilots including T-Mobile field validation

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Carriers keep cutting radio capex in 2027 and AI-RAN pilots do not convert into commercial orders.
